::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
This list is compiled and ranked each month by Claude, an AI model made by
Anthropic, running unattended. No person reviews the entries or the scores
before they are published. Andy Stein sets the criteria in
[Specification 2](specification2-curated-list.qmd) and does not adjust
individual scores.
:::

Every score runs from 0 to 100. The full definitions are in
[Specification 2](specification2-curated-list.qmd), Section 4.
The scores capture:

- **S** The total of the other scores.
- **Q** Quality
- **E** Expertise
- **M** Maintenance and usability 
- **U** Usage 

Grouping:

- Only skills with evidence of use are ranked.
- **Flags.** ❌ a major error found. ⚠️ no licence, archived repository, authors
  not found in OpenAlex, or an author matched by name alone.
- **At most three skills per library are ranked in each category.** 

## Tool Skills

Skills for particular software tools (e.g. NONMEM, Monolix, nlmixr2)

::: {#tool-skills}
:::

## Task Skills

Skills whose instructions hold across tools (e.g. Model Evaluation)

::: {#task-skills}
:::

## Unproven

Skills scored on everything except use, in order of their total, with no
evidence yet that anyone outside their authors has used them. A skill moves up
to the ranked tables in the month that evidence appears.

::: {#unproven}
:::

## Evaluation Resources

Test cases and benchmarks for measuring how well an assistant does
pharmacometrics work. Not ranked: Specification 2 does not yet define a quality
score for them.

::: {#evaluation-resources}
:::

## This Month's Run

**November 2026**, run on 2026-11-01 under criteria version 2. Five of the 53
scored skills have evidence of use and are ranked. The data are in
[`list/2026-11.yml`](https://github.com/iamstein/TrinityMetrics/blob/main/projects/ai-pmx-skills-modeling-guidance/list/2026-11.yml),
and the queries with their hit counts in
[`discovery.yml`](https://github.com/iamstein/TrinityMetrics/blob/main/projects/ai-pmx-skills-modeling-guidance/discovery.yml).

**Both known-answer checks passed.** The error audit reported both errors in
[`fixtures.yml`](https://github.com/iamstein/TrinityMetrics/blob/main/projects/ai-pmx-skills-modeling-guidance/fixtures.yml)
as major before anything was scored.

**Nine skills were added**, all under Unproven: nlmixr2llm's new `design`
skill, RConsortium's `admiral-adpc`, namlink's `pbpk-apriori`, NVIDIA's
`nvqsp`, Google's `in-vivo-pk-analysis`, X-Science's `dmpk-adme-strategy`,
tamir-agent-skills' `pharmacokinetic-modeling`, aira's
`co-scientist-clinical-pharmacology` and MathWorks' `simbiology-build-model`.
None was removed. The nlmixr2llm repository moved to the nlmixr2 organisation.

**Ranks changed in the tool table.** Three skills changed by 10 or more points:

- **nlmixr2llm `interop`** rose from 3rd to 1st (40.4 to 58.2). This month's
  second judge and tie-break counted its hand-offs to other skills and found
  that continuous integration runs three of its reference-file examples, which
  October's single pass did not.
- **nlmixr2llm `estimation`** fell from 1st to 3rd (51.0 to 27.8). The audit
  rated two of its rules major errors: removing an ETA because between-subject
  variability exceeds 100%, and removing one because shrinkage exceeds 30%.
  Its expertise score also fell from 52 to 13, because Matthew Fidler now wrote
  75% of its lines and OpenAlex could not be reached to score him.
- **nlmixr2lib `extract-literature-model`** fell from 47.6 to 21.9, still
  Unproven. The audit found four major errors in its NONMEM translation rules,
  among them a `S1 = V/1000` rule that puts concentrations out by a factor of
  1,000.

All three sets of errors were in the October files, which October's single
audit scored. Unchanged skills keep October's answers, so they have had one
audit and the rescored skills two.

**The two rubric judges agreed on 88% of items** (153 of 174), across the 18
skills rescored this month. Three items fell below the 85% threshold: R1, R7
and R8. A third judge decided all 21 disagreements.

**OpenAlex was unreachable from the run.** Contributors added since October,
and the authors of the nine new skills, score 0 on expertise and carry the
⚠️ authors-not-found flag until a run can look them up.

This run departs from the specification in four further ways. All are listed
in the data file's `run` block:

1. **All passes used one model.** The rubric's two judges, the tie-break and
   the error audit all ran on the same model, where Section 4.1 asks for the
   audit to use a different one. The test-retest correlation was not produced.
2. **No benchmark score.** The nlmixr2llm vitals evaluation and RConsortium's
   `admiral-adpc` benchmark now cover listed skills with expected answers.
   Running them needs model access and R, which the run did not have.
3. **Use is measured from the authors of issues and pull requests**, found by
   GitHub search. Commenters and GitHub Discussions were not read.
4. **Large libraries were not read skill by skill.** Only the skills that the
   discovery terms matched were considered.

## Proposed Changes to the Criteria

The run proposes these for Andy to accept or reject in [`criteria.yml`](https://github.com/iamstein/TrinityMetrics/blob/main/projects/ai-pmx-skills-modeling-guidance/criteria.yml) and
[`rubric.md`](https://github.com/iamstein/TrinityMetrics/blob/main/projects/ai-pmx-skills-modeling-guidance/rubric.md). Until he does, the criteria stay as they are.

1. **Add a rubric item for domain content.** A templated review skill with no
   named diagnostic meets most of the current items, so it scores close to a
   skill that explains how to read a VPC. An item such as "names at least five
   specific diagnostics or methods and says how to read each" would separate
   them.
2. **Add a rubric item for verified output.** Some tool skills require the
   assistant to check its result numerically before reporting it, such as a
   converted model reproducing the original engine's predictions. The rubric
   gives that no credit.
3. **Define a score for evaluation resources**, from the number of test cases
   with expected answers and the tasks they cover, so the third category can be
   ranked.
4. **Decide how organisations count for expertise.** Skills published under an
   organisation or a bot account score 0 on E, however expert the team. A
   named-author list, where the organisation publishes one, could stand in.
5. **Reword R1.** The judges agreed on 67% of R1 answers. Say whether handing
   named work to another skill counts as stating what the skill does not do,
   and whether a statement of what the underlying software cannot do counts.
   This run counted the first and not the second.
6. **Reword R7.** The judges agreed on 78% of R7 answers, splitting on command
   templates with placeholder inputs. Say whether an example must run on
   bundled or public data as written.
7. **Reword R8.** The judges agreed on 83% of R8 answers. Say whether
   continuous integration that renders the skill's outputs, or runs only some
   of its examples, counts.
8. **Re-audit unchanged skills every three months**, alongside expertise.
   This month two skills gained major errors that were in their files in
   October. Their unchanged neighbours have had only October's single audit.
